subject: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request
messages:
From: Kelsey Tran <kelsey.tran@medicorehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicorehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the runtime throughput numbers. Our security team has a follow-up: before we start procurement they need a short "cut-sheet" that summarizes exactly where customer data may be processed, how VPC/private deployments are isolated, and a high-level ops contact list for runbook escalation.

Specifically they want:
- A one-page summary of residency scope (US vs EU vs APAC) and whether any tokens/metadata may touch non-designated regions.
- A VPC/private-deploy ops snippet describing private endpoint topology, expected network egress paths, and keystore ownership (customer vs Redwood).
- A point of contact (name + role + email) for on-call during install and for SOC2/document requests.

Can you send a short packet we can attach to the RFP by EOD your time? If you have a pre-made template that covers SOC 2 references (section numbers we can cite) that would be ideal.

Kelsey
Kelsey Tran
Senior Security Program Manager
Medicore Health

[Attachment: example_questionnaire_from_medicore.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request

Team — forwarding a Medicore ask (see attached). They need a concise consumer-facing summary + an ops snippet we can ship with procurement. Goal: < 1 page residency summary + 1 page VPC ops excerpt + SOC2 section refs.

Two quick asks:
1) Marissa — can you produce a one-page residency cut-sheet that calls out: supported regions (US/EU/APAC), data-at-rest KMS partitions, and any optional cross-region failover behavior? Keep language customer-facing."

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request

Thanks Irene — I can draft the cut-sheet. Quick clarifying notes:
- For default hosted customers we document "data may be processed in region where model serving occurs"; for Dedicated/Private we call out customer-controlled regions and optional standby regions for disaster recovery.
- Keystore ownership: Private deployments can be configured with customer KMS (recommended), Dedicated uses customer KMS in most customers; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS with customer CMKs available for enterprise.

I'll attach:
- residency_scope_cut_sheet_v1.pdf (one-pager)
- vpc_ops_runbook_excerpt.docx (ops snippet, 1 page)
- redwood-soc2-section-reference.txt (list of SOC2 section numbers and corresponding artifacts)

I put conservative language around "no customer plaintext leaves designated regions" but included the standard fallback: in rare cross-region failover (manual DR) logs/metrics may transit. If you want stronger wording we can escalate to Legal.

Marissa
Director, Product Trust
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request

Adding a couple of technical clarifications for the ops snippet:
- Private deploy topology: customer VPC <-> Private Link endpoint <-> attachment to on-prem/dedicated subnet. We call out that routing is strictly ingress-initiated by the customer (no persistent cross-region egress).
- KV/Key handling: we include an example KMS partition map and an ops play that shows key rotate + emergency-rekey process (customer-owned key recommended for regulated data).
- Audit evidence: point them to SOC2 artifact set (Logs: access.log, operator actions) and SIG/CAIQ answers already mapped to the runbook.

I'll add a short table to vpc_ops_runbook_excerpt.docx with port/listener expectations and expected CIDR annotations.

Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Tran <kelsey.tran@medicorehealth.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medicorehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Residency scope / VPC ops cut-sheet request

Hi Kelsey — attaching the short packet per your ask. Summary below and attachments included.

Executive summary (one-line): Redwood supports hosted, Dedicated (reserved pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments; customer production data remains within customer-designated regions except in customer-authorized cross-region failover or manual troubleshooting scenarios.

What we attached:
- residency_scope_cut_sheet_v1.pdf — one-page customer-ready summary covering US/EU/APAC coverage, optional standby regions, and high-level KMS ownership options.
- vpc_ops_runbook_excerpt.docx — 1-page ops snippet describing PrivateLink topology, expected ingress-only peering, sample CIDRs, and port expectations.
- redwood-soc2-section-reference.txt — quick map of SOC2 sections and where Medicore can find the artifacts in our evidence portal.

Notes / callouts:
- Keystore ownership: for Private we recommend customer-managed KMS (we provide integration patterns), Dedicated supports CMK bring-your-own, hosted offers Redwood-managed keys with enterprise CMK option.
- Cross-region failover: by default we do not route production traffic across regions; DR procedures that temporarily move workloads are documented in the DR appendix and require customer sign-off.
- Evidence: if Medicore needs SOC2 artifact access we can provide a limited-time evidence bundle and controlled read-only viewer.

Next steps: If this looks good I can send a DocuSign link for a narrow terms appendix to cover standby-region behavior and evidence access. If your security team needs tighter language we can route to Legal for a binding residency statement.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Trust Programs
Redwood Inference
